page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-4800s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built for memory-intensive and large-footprint data tasks. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, the instance provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading. It features 192 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of an integrated 4800 GB NVMe SSD array. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity and exceptional large-block memory bandwidth. In stress-ng, the server scored 2,929.87 in single-core and 69,533.1 in multi-core metrics, positioning it within the top 25% of evaluated systems. Large-block uncached memory operations reached the top 10% tier, showing read bandwidth of 488.87 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 225.61 GB/sec. PassMark testing further validated its raw computation, earning a CPU score of 51,801.15 and an extended instructions score of 60,674.26, both landing in the top 25% bracket.

General application tasks fall within mid-tier performance thresholds. Geekbench yielded a single-core score of 1,837.0 and a multi-core score of 14,950.0. Operational tests demonstrated 55.54 million Redis SET operations per second and 18.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound small-model LLM inference generated 258.77 tokens per second on a 135M model, dropping to 26.84 tokens per second on a 7B model. While adequate for CPU-driven analysis, lack of dedicated accelerators limits large model efficiency.

The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and large bundled NVMe storage provide high density without the overhead of external disk attachments. This balance suits in-memory databases, large-scale ETL pipelines, data analytics workloads, and high-capacity database systems that require persistent local fast storage alongside substantial memory headroom.
